findings.name: "Limit of Uses" accepts decimals and silently saves a truncated number (1.5 → 1, 2.9 → 2)
findings.summary: The decimal is accepted without any message: the field, \"Uses left\" and the Redemptions panel show the fractional value (\"0 of 1.5 used\", \"1.5 redemptions left\"). After Save the stored and displayed value is silently truncated to a whole number — 1.5 becomes 1, 2.9 becomes 2 — with no error, warning or notice, so the voucher ends up with a different cap than the one entered. (on /discounts/vouchers/Vm91Y2hlcjoxMg%3D%3D (Limits section) — same field on /discounts/vouchers/add)
findings.expected: A total redemption cap is a whole number of redemptions: the field should refuse 1.5 and 2.9 with a message (like it does for 0: \"Enter a limit of at least 1.\"), or round to a whole number with a visible statement of what was saved — never accept the value, show it in the summary, then store a different number after Save.
findings.actual: The decimal is accepted without any message: the field, \"Uses left\" and the Redemptions panel show the fractional value (\"0 of 1.5 used\", \"1.5 redemptions left\"). After Save the stored and displayed value is silently truncated to a whole number — 1.5 becomes 1, 2.9 becomes 2 — with no error, warning or notice, so the voucher ends up with a different cap than the one entered.
reproSteps: Open https://5503-iczexfc5c5jr1740fp5kf.e2b.app/discounts/vouchers/Vm91Y2hlcjoxMg%3D%3D (the voucher "agent7-limit"; any voucher with "Limit number of times this discount can be used in total" available works).
In the left section menu click "Limits" and turn on "Limit number of times this discount can be used in total".
In the "Limit of Uses" field clear the value and type 1.5.
Look at the field, the "Uses left" figure next to it and the right-hand Redemptions panel: they read 1.5 ("0 of 1.5 used", "1.5 redemptions left").
Click Save and wait for "Voucher updated".
Read the field and the panel again: the limit is now 1 ("1 redemption left"). Repeat with 2.9: it is accepted as 2.9 and saved as 2.

findings.name: Saving with an empty Start Date silently overwrites it with now and discards the Start Hour the user entered
findings.summary: Start Date becomes today's date 11/24/2026 and Start Hour becomes the current clock time (12:24 AM in the first run, 12:34 AM in the second) — the hour that was on screen (10:00 AM / 11:59 AM) is thrown away. Nothing warns the user; a green 'Voucher updated' toast is shown, and only then can they see the schedule was replaced. (on /discounts/vouchers/Vm91Y2hlcjo1)
findings.expected: Either the schedule should not accept a Start Hour without a Start Date, or, if the start has to be filled in on save, the app should keep the hour the user entered (11:59 AM) and say plainly what was stored (or leave the start unset and say so).
findings.actual: Start Date becomes today's date 11/24/2026 and Start Hour becomes the current clock time (12:24 AM in the first run, 12:34 AM in the second) — the hour that was on screen (10:00 AM / 11:59 AM) is thrown away. Nothing warns the user; a green 'Voucher updated' toast is shown, and only then can they see the schedule was replaced.
reproSteps: Open the voucher detail page https://5503-iczexfc5c5jr1740fp5kf.e2b.app/discounts/vouchers/Vm91Y2hlcjo1 (signed in as admin@example.com).

Click Save at the bottom right and watch the two Start fields.
Read the Schedule panel: Start Date is now 11/24/2026 and Start Hour 12:34 AM (the current time), not the 11:59 AM that was on screen; a green 'Voucher updated' toast is shown.
